narrative: Material PL1__M5B2BEA9 exhibits variable demand (CV=0.64, mean 471 units/day) with 12.6% zero-demand days and no significant trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.60, mean 1.38 days) with episodic multi-day deliveries that dominate the uncertainty budget (54.6%). An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ order quantity is recommended; the current SAP policy orders at MOQ=589 approximately 200 times/year, whereas the optimised policy consolidates to ~14 orders/year at 8,589 units, saving $13,307 (87.8%) annually while holding a 95% service level.
warnings: Order quantity capped at storage limit: max_storage_units (9448) - safety_stock (859) = 8589, binding capacity constraint active.
Lead time CV=0.60 is high; supplier consistency improvement recommended to reduce required safety stock.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is largely continuous (87.4% non-zero) with high variability, making a continuous-review policy superior to periodic review. The EOQ minimises total ordering and holding cost; the reorder point provides statistical coverage against combined demand and lead-time uncertainty at the 95% service level. MOQ=589 is non-binding as EOQ=8,589 exceeds it significantly.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint: the recommended policy places maximum inventory at exactly 9,448 units (= 859 SS + 8,589 OQ), equal to the storage limit. Any upward revision of safety stock (e.g., for higher service level) would require a proportional reduction in order quantity, increasing ordering frequency and cost. Lead time CV=0.60 is the primary uncertainty driver; improving supplier consistency would release storage headroom.
